title: Acute diarrhoea with dehydration in children (India, IAP)
subject: paediatrics
setting: Home, primary care, clinic, emergency department, ward
summary: Classify dehydration, rehydrate with low osmolarity ORS (Plan A at home, Plan B 75 mL/kg over 4 hours) or Ringer lactate for severe dehydration (Plan C), give zinc for 14 days, keep feeding, and reserve antibiotics for dysentery, cholera and other specific indications.

sections.title: Define and classify dehydration
items: Acute watery diarrhoea: loose or liquid stools and/or 3 or more stools in 24 hours, with or without fever or vomiting, lasting 7 days or less (IAP). ICMR: acute below 14 days, persistent 14 days or more, dysentery if blood in stool. Frequent formed stools, and pasty stools of exclusively breastfed babies, are not diarrhoea.

Severe dehydration (at least 2): lethargic or unconscious, sunken eyes, unable to drink or drinking poorly, skin pinch goes back very slowly (2 seconds or more). Deficit over 10% of body weight (over 100 mL/kg): Plan C.
Some dehydration (2 or more): restless and irritable, sunken eyes, drinks eagerly and thirsty. Deficit 5 to 10% (50 to 100 mL/kg): Plan B.
No dehydration: not enough signs for some or severe. Deficit below 5%: Plan A at home.

Ask about blood in stool, duration, vomiting, fever, recent measles, HIV status, immunisation, feeding and remedies already given. Check weight, weight for height or MUAC and classify malnutrition, because SAM changes rehydration (see special section).

Most children need no tests. Severe dehydration: CBC, electrolytes, renal function, blood glucose (and venous blood gas if available). Stool microbiology only for chronic illness or immunodeficiency, sepsis, symptoms over 7 days, outbreaks, high fever or travel to at-risk areas.

sections.title: Plan C: severe dehydration
items: Start IV Ringer lactate at once (0.9% saline or half-strength Darrow solution if RL is unavailable). If the child can drink, give ORS by mouth while the drip is set up.
Infants under 12 months: 30 mL/kg over 1 hour, then 70 mL/kg over 5 hours.
Children over 1 year: 30 mL/kg over 30 minutes, then 70 mL/kg over 2 and a half hours.

Reassess every 15 to 30 minutes until a strong radial pulse is present, then hourly; if hydration is not improving, run the drip faster. Start ORS about 5 mL/kg/h as soon as the child can drink (usually after 3 to 4 hours in infants, 1 to 2 hours in older children).

Reclassify after 6 hours (infants) or 3 hours (older children) and continue with Plan A, B or C. If IV access is not possible, rehydrate by nasogastric tube and refer urgently, with the mother giving frequent sips of ORS on the way.
Recognise early shock (heart rate, respiratory rate, BP, capillary refill, consciousness) and refer for admission; observe for at least 6 hours after full rehydration.

sections.title: Plan B: some dehydration
items: ORS 75 mL/kg over 4 hours in the clinic or day-care facility, in frequent small sips by spoon or cup; if the child vomits, wait 10 minutes and continue more slowly.

If weight is unknown (ICMR 4-hour ORS volumes): under 4 months (below 5 kg) 200 to 400 mL; 4 to 11 months (5 to 7.9 kg) 400 to 600 mL; 12 to 23 months (8 to 10.9 kg) 600 to 800 mL; 2 to 4 years (11 to 15.9 kg) 800 to 1200 mL; 5 to 14 years (16 to 29.9 kg) 1200 to 2200 mL; 15 years or older (30 kg or more) 2200 to 4000 mL.
Continue breastfeeding. Non-breastfed infants under 6 months also get 100 to 200 mL of clean water during Plan B; older children free access to plain water.
Monitor hourly and reassess after 4 hours: repeat Plan B if still some dehydration, move to Plan A if rehydrated, Plan C if worse. Check electrolytes if available.
Children who fail oral rehydration can be rehydrated by nasogastric tube or IV.

sections.title: Plan A, zinc, feeding and adjuncts
items: Plan A (home): low osmolarity ORS (sodium 75 mmol/L) after every loose stool, 10 mL/kg, or by age: up to 2 months 5 teaspoons; 2 months to under 2 years 50 to 100 mL; 2 to 10 years 100 to 200 mL; older children as much as they want. Check on the packet whether it is made up in 200 mL or 1 litre.
Zinc for 14 days: 10 mg/day for infants 2 to 6 months, 20 mg/day from 6 months to 5 years. It shortens the episode and reduces diarrhoea over the next 3 months.
Ondansetron 0.15 mg/kg per dose orally or IV (maximum 8 mg) for vomiting that blocks oral rehydration.
Selected probiotic strains (Lactobacillus rhamnosus GG, Saccharomyces boulardii, L. reuteri DSM 17938) may be added to ORS; they do not replace it.

Feeding: continue breastfeeding (more often than usual); do not dilute or change formula; restart normal food no later than 4 to 6 hours after rehydration begins. Home fluids: salted rice water or dal water, vegetable soup, salted lassi, shikanji with salt and less sugar, coconut water.
Avoid carbonated drinks, commercial fruit juices and sweetened tea or coffee. Give one extra meal a day for 1 to 2 weeks after the diarrhoea stops, or until the child regains the original weight.

sections.title: Antibiotics: only for specific indications
items: No routine antibiotics for acute watery diarrhoea. Consider them in infants under 3 months, chronic illness or immunodeficiency, SAM, invasive bacterial infection, or proven Shigella, enterotoxigenic E. coli, Vibrio cholerae or Yersinia.
Shigella or dysentery (IAP): ceftriaxone 50 mg/kg IV or IM for 2 to 5 days; oral alternatives cefixime 8 mg/kg/day or ciprofloxacin 20 to 30 mg/kg/day.

Dysentery (ICMR, outpatient): ciprofloxacin 15 mg/kg twice daily and review at 2 days; if better complete 3 days. If not better, cefixime 10 mg/kg/day in 2 divided doses, review after 2 days and complete 3 to 5 days. Refer if still no improvement.
Cholera: single dose doxycycline 2 to 4 mg/kg (over 2 years), or single dose azithromycin or ciprofloxacin 20 mg/kg.

Enterotoxigenic E. coli: azithromycin 10 mg/kg/day for 3 days (alternative cefixime 8 mg/kg/day for 5 days). Non-typhoidal Salmonella only in high-risk children: ceftriaxone 50 to 100 mg/kg/day (alternatives azithromycin 10 mg/kg/day or ciprofloxacin 20 to 30 mg/kg/day).
Amoebic trophozoites on stool microscopy: metronidazole 10 mg/kg per dose 8-hourly for 7 days (10 days if severe). Giardia: metronidazole 5 mg/kg per dose 8-hourly for 5 to 7 days.

sections.title: Diarrhoea in severe acute malnutrition
items: Diagnose dehydration from history (sudden-onset diarrhoea, recent change in appearance, eyes newly sunken, eagerness to drink); the usual signs are unreliable in SAM. Manage in a health facility.
Shock in SAM: cold hands with capillary refill over 3 seconds and a weak, fast pulse. IV fluids only for shock, because of the risk of overhydration and heart failure.

Otherwise rehydrate orally or by nasogastric tube slowly: 70 to 100 mL/kg over 12 hours, starting at 10 mL/kg/h for the first 2 hours, then alternating hours with starter diet; adjust to thirst and ongoing losses. Increasing oedema means overhydration.

Do not use full-strength ORS (too much sodium, too little potassium). Modified ORS: 1 packet of 75 mmol/L ORS in 2 litres of water plus 45 mL potassium chloride solution (from a 100 g/L stock) and 50 g sucrose; or ReSoMal.
See the severe acute malnutrition protocol for the remaining steps (hypoglycaemia, hypothermia, infection, feeding).

sections.title: Refer, discharge and follow up
items: Refer to hospital (ICMR): severe dehydration; SAM or HIV; hypernatraemic (sodium above 145 mmol/L) or hyponatraemic (below 135 mmol/L) dehydration; dysentery under 1 year, after measles in the past 6 weeks, with dehydration, or not improving on antibiotics; persistent diarrhoea with dehydration, serious systemic infection, age under 4 months or no improvement in 5 days.
Discharge when rehydrated (weight gain and/or clinical status), IV fluids are no longer needed, oral intake equals or exceeds losses, and follow-up is available.
Teach danger signs to return at once: many watery stools, repeated vomiting, very thirsty, eating or drinking poorly, fever, or blood in the stool. Review in 5 days if not improving.
Prevention: hand washing, safe water, sanitary disposal of faeces, and up-to-date immunisation, especially rotavirus and measles.

sections.title: Pitfalls
items: Giving antibiotics or antimotility drugs for simple watery diarrhoea.
Stopping feeds or diluting milk during diarrhoea.
Rapid IV fluids or standard ORS in a child with SAM.
Forgetting zinc, or stopping it when the diarrhoea settles instead of completing 14 days.
Missing hypernatraemic dehydration, where the child looks less ill than the deficit suggests.

drugs.name: Low osmolarity ORS (sodium 75 mmol/L)
drugs.dose: Plan A: 10 mL/kg (or 50 to 100 mL under 2 years, 100 to 200 mL at 2 to 10 years) after each loose stool. Plan B: 75 mL/kg over 4 hours
drugs.notes: First-line for all dehydration short of shock. Modified dilution in SAM.

drugs.name: Ringer lactate
drugs.dose: Infant: 30 mL/kg over 1 hour then 70 mL/kg over 5 hours. Over 1 year: 30 mL/kg over 30 minutes then 70 mL/kg over 2.5 hours
drugs.notes: Plan C. Normal saline if RL unavailable. Not for SAM without shock.

drugs.name: Zinc
drugs.dose: 2 to 6 months: 10 mg/day; 6 months to 5 years: 20 mg/day; for 14 days

drugs.name: Ondansetron
drugs.dose: 0.15 mg/kg per dose orally or IV, maximum 8 mg

drugs.name: Ceftriaxone
drugs.dose: Shigella: 50 mg/kg IV or IM daily for 2 to 5 days. High-risk non-typhoidal Salmonella: 50 to 100 mg/kg/day
drugs.notes: Parenteral first choice for invasive or severe dysentery.

drugs.name: Ciprofloxacin
drugs.dose: 15 mg/kg twice daily for 3 days (ICMR dysentery); IAP alternative 20 to 30 mg/kg/day
drugs.notes: Review at 48 hours; switch if no improvement.

drugs.name: Cefixime
drugs.dose: 8 mg/kg/day (IAP) or 10 mg/kg/day in 2 divided doses (ICMR) for 3 to 5 days

drugs.name: Azithromycin
drugs.dose: 10 mg/kg/day for 3 days (ETEC); single dose 20 mg/kg for cholera
drugs.notes: Also an alternative for high-risk non-typhoidal Salmonella (10 mg/kg/day).

drugs.name: Metronidazole
drugs.dose: Amoebiasis: 10 mg/kg per dose 8-hourly for 7 to 10 days. Giardiasis: 5 mg/kg per dose 8-hourly for 5 to 7 days
drugs.notes: Only when trophozoites or cysts are seen.
